title: The review check becomes a reusable workflow
summary: The review check moves out of osf's own `review.yml` into a reusable `review-check.yml` that any repository can call. The caller is now one job with no steps: it passes `osf-ref` (the workflow's own commit), the runner label, the verifier app id and `allow-forks`, and inherits secrets. The build job no longer compiles the pull request's base branch — it checks out the pinned osf commit, refuses anything that is not the workflow's own commit and repository, and builds it read-only into a separate `build-out`. On the osf side, `review reduce` now accepts a folder of saved reviewer files instead of a file list, and a pull request file may be a raw code-host event file.

lanes.label: Caller
lanes.subtitle: pull_request_target, default branch
lanes.summary: The workflow GitHub reads from the default branch. It holds no step of its own and cannot be changed by a pull request.

lanes.label: Review check
lanes.subtitle: reusable workflow jobs
lanes.summary: The reusable workflow that holds every job: build, one job per reviewer, the last job that decides and posts, and the fork-disabled failure.

lanes.label: osf binary
lanes.subtitle: Rust CLI, built from the pinned commit
lanes.summary: The tool the jobs run. It finds the work item, runs one reviewer, and reduces the saved answers into a decision.

lanes.label: External
lanes.subtitle: GitHub, providers, registry
lanes.summary: The code host, the model providers, and the container registry the jobs reach over the network.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: one job, no steps
nodes.summary: osf's own caller. It triggers on `pull_request_target` and does nothing but call the reusable workflow by local path, passing `github.workflow_sha` as `osf-ref` and reading the adopter's variables for the runner, the verifier app id and fork review.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: on: workflow_call
nodes.summary: The reusable workflow. It declares the stable inputs and secrets, pins the review image by digest, and holds every job. A caller in another repository names it by full commit SHA.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.subtitle: no secret, read-only token
nodes.summary: Checks out the pinned osf commit, refuses any ref that is not a full SHA or not the workflow's own commit and repository, builds it with no cache into `build-out`, and finds the work item with a read-only token. It never checks out the pull request's code.

nodes.label: reviewer jobs
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude, opencode
nodes.summary: One job per reviewer, each holding only its own provider key from the `review` environment and an egress list of its provider's hosts. Each mounts the base and the pull request read-only and runs `osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled`.

nodes.label: review job
nodes.subtitle: decides and posts
nodes.summary: The last job. It downloads every reviewer's saved answers, mints the verifier app's token, and runs `osf review reduce` over the folder of runs. It runs even when a reviewer job failed, and a reviewer with no saved answers counts as could-not-run.

nodes.label: review-fork-disabled
nodes.subtitle: fails loudly
nodes.summary: A fork's pull request with `allow-forks` false lands here and fails, rather than skipping, so an unconfigured fork review cannot pass the check by accident.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: cargo build --release --bin osf
nodes.summary: The review CLI. The build job compiles it from the pinned commit and uploads it as an artifact; every later job downloads that one binary.

nodes.label: review run
nodes.subtitle: one reviewer, one process
nodes.summary: Runs a single reviewer in the container and saves its answers. It now notes by name when a selected reviewer's credential variable is empty or unset, so the run counts as could-not-run instead of silently failing to sign in.

nodes.label: review reduce
nodes.subtitle: collect, check, decide, post
nodes.summary: Collects the saved reviewer files, checks the findings against the pull request's files, decides, writes SARIF and posts. It now expands a folder argument into the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name.

nodes.label: review context
nodes.subtitle: PullRequest::load
nodes.summary: Reads the pull request from a JSON file. It now accepts either the flat number/title/body file or a code-host event file that nests them under `pull_request`, so a job can pass the event file straight through.

nodes.label: review_workflow tests
nodes.subtitle: reads the workflow as text
nodes.summary: Checks the reusable workflow and the caller as text: the stable input list, the declared secrets, the pinned commit guard, the fixed environment names, the single verifier token mint, and that the caller is thin.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.subtitle: api.github.com
nodes.summary: The code host. It serves the event, the checkouts, the artifacts and the review post, and reports `job.workflow_sha` and `job.workflow_repository` to the build job.

nodes.label: Model providers
nodes.subtitle: openai, anthropic, openrouter
nodes.summary: Each reviewer job reaches only its own provider's host, plus the hosts its agent needs to start.

nodes.label: ghcr.io
nodes.subtitle: review image by digest
nodes.summary: The container registry. Every job logs in with its own token and pulls the same review image, pinned by digest and named once in the workflow.

edges.label: uses: review-check.yml
edges.summary: The caller's one job calls the reusable workflow, passing the stable inputs and `secrets: inherit`.

edges.label: cargo build --release
edges.summary: The build job compiles osf from the pinned commit inside the review image, with no cache, and uploads the binary as an artifact.

edges.label: osf review work-item
edges.summary: With a read-only token, the build job runs `osf review work-item` against the event file to find the issue the pull request names.

edges.label: osf review run --reviewer
edges.summary: Each reviewer job runs one reviewer in the container, with only its own provider key in the environment.

edges.label: osf review reduce /out/runs
edges.summary: The last job passes the folder of downloaded reviewer answers to `osf review reduce`, which expands it into the `.json` files inside.

edges.label: PullRequest::load
edges.summary: The reduce path loads the pull request through the shared loader, so an event file works as well as a flat file.

edges.label: provider API
edges.summary: Each reviewer job's egress list allows only its own provider's host, so a reviewer cannot reach another provider.

edges.label: docker pull by digest
edges.summary: Every job logs in to ghcr.io and runs the same image, pinned by digest and named once in the workflow's env block.

edges.label: check run + review
edges.summary: The last job alone mints the verifier app's token and posts the check run and the review.

edges.label: event + work item
edges.summary: The build job reads the event and the named issue with a token limited to issues and pull requests.

edges.label: reads as text
edges.summary: The workflow tests read `review-check.yml` and `review.yml` as text and assert the input list, the secrets, the pin guard and the caller's shape.

flows.title: One review run, from caller to posted review
flows.summary: A pull request event reaches the caller, which calls the reusable workflow. The build job compiles the pinned osf and finds the work item; each reviewer job runs one reviewer; the last job reduces the saved answers and posts.

messages.label: workflow_call: osf-ref, runs-on, verifier-app-id, allow-forks
messages.note: The caller passes `github.workflow_sha` as `osf-ref`, so the osf that runs is the commit of the workflow itself, never the pull request's base.

messages.label: cargo build --release --bin osf
messages.note: The build runs inside the review image against the read-only `osf-src` checkout, writing to a separate `build-out` folder.

messages.label: osf review work-item
messages.note: A read-only token finds the issue the pull request names, and the result is uploaded as the `work-item` artifact.

messages.label: osf-binary + work-item artifacts
messages.note: Each reviewer job downloads the one binary and the work item, and mounts the base and the pull request read-only.

messages.label: osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled
messages.note: The reviewer runs in the container with only its own provider key. An empty key is noted by name and counts as could-not-run.

messages.label: review-run-<name> artifact
messages.note: Each reviewer job uploads its saved answers even when it failed, so the last job can count a missing answer as could-not-run.

messages.label: osf review reduce /out/runs
messages.note: The folder stands for the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name, so the workflow lists no file.

messages.label: check run + review
messages.note: The last job alone mints the verifier app's token and posts the decision.
